This chapter is the map of snapy for a reader who has never opened it. It follows one time step from the caller's
loop, through a `MeshBlock` or a `Mesh`, into the hydro and scalar kernels, and back out to the written outputs. It
then says where the data lives in memory, how a run is configured, how Python reaches the same objects, and which
external packages the code leans on. Every section is a code map read at the pin of `code_pin.yml`. It names the
function that does each thing and the test that holds the claim up. It makes no new numerical claim of its own. The
physics of each operator belongs to its own chapter, which the map points at. The directories and modules of the repository, with the chapter
that covers each, are listed in @sec-appj.

The dependency figure below is a call-ownership map: an arrow says who calls what, not that one numerical
switch implies another. The switch couplings are in @sec-ch12-matrix.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch01-overview-dependencies
#| fig-cap: "Interfaces around Mesh and MeshBlock. Black arrows associate the block API with its caller, increment operators, exchange layout and external services; they do not assert a numerical switch implication."
#| fig-alt: "Mesh or MeshBlock linked to its caller, hydro and scalar, layout, and external integrator and thermodynamics."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch01.fig_overview_dependencies import make_fig
make_fig()
```
